
SAShiny lets an **unchanged SAS program** act as the server of a Shiny app. A
sidecar YAML contract declares the program's inputs and outputs; SAShiny
validates the inputs, safely passes them to SAS as macro variables, submits the
program verbatim, and collects the results.

This vignette walks through the core workflow using the **mock engine**, which
needs no SAS installation.

## The contract

A SAShiny program is a pair of files:

- `analysis.sas` — your SAS program (never modified).
- `analysis.sashiny.yml` — the contract declaring inputs and outputs.

```{r}
library(SAShiny)

# Write a minimal contract and program to a temporary directory.
dir <- tempfile("sashiny-")
dir.create(dir)
writeLines(c(
  "sashiny: 1",
  "program: program.sas",
  "title: Minimal",
  "outputs:",
  "  log:",
  "    type: log"
), file.path(dir, "contract.sashiny.yml"))
writeLines("proc print data=sashelp.class; run;", file.path(dir, "program.sas"))
```

## Load and validate

```{r}
contract <- sas_contract(file.path(dir, "contract.sashiny.yml"))
issues <- sas_validate(contract)
length(issues)  # 0 means valid
```

## Run against the mock engine

```{r}
engine <- sas_engine_mock()
result <- sas_run(contract, list(), engine)
result$status
```

## Connection selection

For live SAS, choose one of three backends. The consumer supplies the connection
details; credentials come from `~/.authinfo`.

```{r}
oda <- sas_connect("oda", region = "us1")
oda$cfg$authkey
```
